trades.headline: Their second quarterback scores them nothing every week, and their flex is a tight end
trades.yourSurplus: Golden is your WR4 behind Rice and Wilson and does not enter the lineup while both are healthy. His 15.5 in week 1 raises his price, so this is harder than it was yesterday.
trades.theirHole: Team 13 roster Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson in a one-quarterback league and start Travis Kelce in their RB/WR/TE flex because no third receiver clears him. Golden fixes the flex; the quarterback they give up never plays.
trades.yourLineup: Allen at quarterback. Worth noting this is now a luxury rather than a need — Lawrence scored 25.6 on your bench while Stafford started and scored 4.1, and he solves the position for free.
trades.theirLineup: They keep Lamar and put Golden in the flex over Kelce.
trades.risk: Golden's 15.5 may have corrected their valuation. Lead with their flex problem, not your quarterback problem. And do not overpay: you no longer need this trade, you would just like it.

candidates.note: 29.8 points and 50% rostered, which is an anomaly in a ten-team league. Still not worth this league's waiver priority, which never resets — he is a flex competing with Tuten, not a starter filling a hole. He clears Wednesday 07:00 UTC. If nobody claims him, add him free.

Carried forward because it still stops a mistake. Hunter shows rank 1 in the data, which reads like the best player on the wire. He is not: Jacksonville list him as a starting cornerback and backup receiver, and he played four offensive snaps in week 1 on one designed touch. The rank is a preseason artifact. Never spend a never-resetting claim on it.
Downgraded again. Bowers is on track to return at the Chargers, which closes the target vacuum that made Tucker interesting after one week.

Irrelevant while you hold Lawrence, but the right shape for week 7 — when Tuten, the Jaguars defence, Cam Little and Lawrence are all out together on the Jacksonville bye. In this league that patch has to be a free agent, never a claim.
